title: Replace the non-Rust file ledger check with a code-in-other-languages ch
summary: Replace the xtask M20 test, which rejects any tracked file kind not listed in docs/non-rust-files.md, with a check that flags code in other languages (by extension or shebang). Data and documents pass anywhere. A short named allow-list covers setup.sh and the CI workflow, each with its reason, and docs/non-rust-files.md describes the new rule.

defaults_applied.how: The check stays a Rust test in xtask, and its purpose is to enforce that all code is Rust.
The new rule gets passing tests, including one that a stray script is still caught. Clippy and fmt must be clean.
The rule stays enforced by a test, not by prose.
The check is rewritten to match the intent (code versus data), not patched with another ledger row for JSON fixtures.
One focused change to the test and its docs.
The docs explain the rule and the reason for each allow-list entry for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The allow-list lives in xtask/tests/policy.rs as a small named const, each entry with a reason string, and docs/non-rust-files.md repeats it as a table.
The CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) is YAML, which is allowed as data, but is still named in the allow-list with its reason because the request asks for it.

Code extensions flagged: py, js, ts, sh, rb, go, plus similar ones (mjs, cjs, jsx, tsx, pl, php, bash, zsh, java, c, cpp, h, lua, ps1). Any text file whose first line starts with #! is also flagged, unless allow-listed.

The existing test names are kept (every_tracked_file_is_rust_or_a_listed_kind may be renamed, with docs/enforcement.md row M20 updated to match) so the M24 check that every named test exists still passes.
Files under owner-private paths stay excluded via the existing athena_files() helper; records/ and the owner's files are not edited.
The new docs text avoids the M19 boundary-scan words.

acceptance_criteria.text: xtask/tests/policy.rs no longer parses the docs/non-rust-files.md table to decide which files are allowed. The M20 check instead flags tracked files with a non-Rust code extension (at least .py, .js, .ts, .sh, .rb, .go) or a shebang first line.
Data and document files (json, toml, yaml, yml, md, txt) pass anywhere in the tree with no ledger entry, including a JSON fixture under a test directory.
A short named allow-list in the test has exactly setup.sh and the CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml), each with a reason string.

docs/non-rust-files.md describes the new rule (code in other languages is flagged, data and documents are allowed, the allow-list has setup.sh and the CI workflow with reasons) and no longer lists per-kind rows for data files. Its notes on the git hooks and the absent schemas and gitleaks files stay accurate.
docs/enforcement.md row M20 names tests that exist in xtask/tests/policy.rs and describes the new rule, and the header comment in policy.rs matches.

A test in xtask/tests/policy.rs shows that a stray script (for example tools/build.py, scripts/run.sh, or an extensionless file with a #!/bin/sh first line) is flagged. It also shows that a JSON fixture, a .md file and a .toml file are not flagged, and that setup.sh is allowed. Run `cargo test -p xtask` and confirm they pass.
`cargo test` passes for the workspace (including M19 and M24 in policy.rs), `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows or .gitattributes.
Rewriting or removing any existing tracked file, or editing records/.
Changing the M19 boundary scan or the M21 dependency-graph check.
departures: Slightly lower cost and higher pass probability than the reference: the change is confined to one test file and its docs, and the repository files that must stay in sync (enforcement.md M20 row, M24 test-name check) are known.
